target.title: feat: show cloud workspace conflicts in the Control UI
target.body:
Related: #110224 (phase 3 of 3; phases 1 and 2 were #110952 and #111244)

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the operator-facing recovery path for cloud workspace conflicts. The Gateway already keeps local versions, applies non-conflicting cloud changes, preserves the cloud result under a staged Git ref, and records the conflict in the session; the Control UI previously left that recovery state hidden in raw placement and transcript data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now turns the existing phase-2 conflict projection into a warning sidebar badge and a dismissible chat notice with a bounded path list, staged-result ref, and copyable inspect/take-cloud commands. The durable custom transcript entry renders as a structured conflict event, so the explanation remains visible after the live placement notice is cleared. No protocol or persistence shape changes are introduced in this phase.

## User Impact

Operators can see that a cloud turn completed with workspace conflicts, identify which local paths were kept, inspect the staged cloud version, and deliberately take that version when appropriate. Non-conflicting cloud changes are already applied, and the UI explains deletion, file/directory obstruction, shell, and stale-ref cases without requiring a blind retry. Retained conflicts remain visible after reclaim and on child-session rows.

## Evidence

- Focused Control UI proof: 3 files passed, 304 tests passed (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/session-row-badges.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts`). The focused Gateway history projection suite also passed 181 tests.
- CI recovery proof: the workflow guard suite passed 86 tests after rotating the poisoned shared dependency snapshot from its v5 lineage to v6 and retiring v5. This prevents hosted jobs from resolving root `ipaddr.js@1.9.1` in place of `packages/net-policy`'s pinned `2.4.0`; the same unrelated failure reproduced on two canonical-main runs before the rotation.
- Conflict-specific browser lifecycle proof on a synced Blacksmith Testbox at head `920bc1fa497`: 1 test passed in 2.53s. It rendered the live notice and sidebar badge, dismissed the notice while retaining structured history, reloaded a positively identified cleared session, and confirmed the badge/notice stayed absent while the durable history card remained. The three screenshot SHA-256 prefixes were `1518bb3a`, `a749df9b`, and `e7c91a4d`. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29684690662)
- Mantis also exercised the candidate Control UI browser shell and published its generic chat screenshot/recording. This is supplemental browser-environment evidence; the conflict-specific behavior is covered by the Testbox lifecycle test above. [Mantis artifacts](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/web-ui-chat-proof/pr-111329/run-29684136714-1/index.json)
- Structured AutoReview (`--mode branch --base origin/main`, Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`) is clean on head `bdfcbc262a4`, with no accepted/actionable findings and overall verdict `patch is correct` (0.91 confidence). The CI repair separately reviewed clean at 0.98, and the added browser test reviewed clean at 0.93 after its refreshed-session readiness race was fixed.
- The rebase retained current-main inline approval cards and approval badges while adding the conflict UI. The landed phase-2 contract remains `workspaceResultConflict` / `cloud-workspace-conflict` with `paths`, `stagedResultRef`, and `totalCount`.

AI-assisted: yes. The rebased diff was reviewed and validated before publication.

target.title: fix: keep newline-mode reply paragraphs as separate channel bubbles
target.body:
Closes #109032

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp users with automatic visible replies and `chunkMode: newline` would see multi-paragraph Codex runtime replies collapse into one bubble, while the same configuration with the OpenClaw runtime kept separate bubbles.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex finals arrive as one accumulated text blob. Shared outbound planning previously packed blank-line paragraphs up to the transport size limit before delivery, so coalescing could not separate them again. The fix stays in the configured delivery path (not the Codex projector):

- `planOutboundTextMessageUnits` with `chunkMode: newline` keeps each blank-line paragraph as its own unit; the transport limit only splits oversized paragraphs.
- `EmbeddedBlockChunker` force flushes with `flushOnParagraph` also preserve those boundaries, so a terminal flush of an under-max buffer does not re-merge paragraphs.

Length-mode delivery is unchanged. No Codex extension import of internal markdown packages.

## User Impact

With WhatsApp (or any channel) `streaming.chunkMode: newline`, multi-paragraph automatic replies from the Codex runtime deliver as separate bubbles, matching OpenClaw runtime behavior. Length-mode and single-paragraph replies are unaffected.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest on Windows 11 (Node v24.15.0), HEAD `5c1fa8fd86`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/outbound/message-plan.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-block-chunker.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts
# Test Files  3 passed (3)
# Tests  83 passed (83)
```

Coverage:

- newline planning keeps two short paragraphs as two outbound units under a 4000-char transport limit
- force + `flushOnParagraph` emits Codex-style multi-paragraph finals as separate chunks
- existing packing defaults for `chunkByParagraph` / `chunkTextWithMode` remain covered by `chunk.test.ts`

Real WhatsApp A/B (distinct outbound message IDs) still needs a live tenant or Mantis capture; unit evidence proves the planning and force-flush boundaries that the reporter A/B attributed to the Codex vs OpenClaw runtime gap.

Prior closed unmerged approach (#109543) split inside the Codex projector and bypassed channel chunk policy; this PR follows ClawSweeper guidance to keep the fix in canonical outbound planning under `chunkMode`.

This PR is AI-assisted (Cursor/Grok).
